Title: TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal trigger route is silent on STM32U5A5JTxQ — DAC sees no triggers despite correct CR config

Body:
# TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal trigger route is silent on STM32U5A5JTxQ — DAC sees no triggers despite correct CR config

**Repository:** STM32CubeU5

**Versions affected:**
- CMSIS device: V1.4.2.0
- HAL: V1.6.x
- Affected chip: STM32U5A5JTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q

**Related upstream issues (same family):**
- [#69](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/issues/69) ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one
- [#70](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/issues/70) LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger silent

This is a third instance of an internal trigger-routing path that is silently silent on this U5A5 silicon — the source generates the event, the destination is correctly configured to receive it, but no event ever reaches the destination. All three involve the chained on-chip trigger paths the U5A5 advertises.

## Severity

metadata.issue_title: TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal trigger route is silent on STM32U5A5JTxQ — DAC sees no triggers despite correct CR config

text:
The standard "TIM1 paces DAC1 via TRGO" pattern — well-supported across the F4 / H7 / G4 families — fails silently on U5A5: DAC1 stops accepting triggers, DOR1 never advances, and any DMA chain feeding DHR1 stalls because the DAC stops requesting refills. No HAL call returns an error.

## Bench reproduction

NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q with a project where:

- DAC1 activated, channel 1 on PA4 (DAC_OUT1).
- hdac1.Init (per CubeMX): DAC_Trigger = DAC_TRIGGER_T1_TRGO, output buffer enabled, no autonomous mode.
- TIM1 configured at 1 kHz (Prescaler = 159, Period = 999) with Init.MasterOutputTrigger = TIM_TRGO_UPDATE (set via HAL_TIMEx_MasterConfigSynchronization).
- DMA chain attached via HAL_DAC_Start_DMA(&hdac1, DAC_CHANNEL_1, sine_table, 100, DAC_ALIGN_12B_R).

Read at runtime:

metadata.issue_title: TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal trigger route is silent on STM32U5A5JTxQ — DAC sees no triggers despite correct CR config

text:
DAC1->CR     = 0x00002007    EN1=1, TEN1=1, TSEL1[0]=1 (TSEL1 = 0001 = TIM1_TRGO per HAL),
                             DMAEN1=1.  All correct per the IOC.
DAC1->DOR1   = 0             stuck at 0 forever — DAC never transferred DHR1 → DOR1.
DAC1->SR     = 0x00000800    BWST = 1 (busy-write-status) — DAC waiting for trigger.
TIM1->CR1    = 0x00000001    counter enabled, ticking at 1 kHz (CNT advancing).
TIM1->CR2    = 0x00000020    MMS = 010 = UPDATE event TRGO source. Verified.
GPDMA1_Ch11.CCR = 0x00005f00   channel disabled (EN=0); CSR=IDLE.
GPDMA1_Ch11.CBR1 = 0x000000be   190 of 200 bytes remaining — only 5 samples
                                 written before the chain stalled because DAC
                                 stopped requesting more.

## Isolation evidence

The same DAC + DMA + trigger setup with the trigger-source field changed in user code:

c
DAC1->CR &= ~(0xFUL << 2);              /* clear TSEL1 */
DAC1->CR |=  (0x8UL << 2) | (1UL << 1); /* TSEL1 = 1000 = TIM15_TRGO, TEN1 = 1 */

metadata.issue_title: TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal trigger route is silent on STM32U5A5JTxQ — DAC sees no triggers despite correct CR config

text:
— *with TIM15 also at 1 kHz Update Event* — produces the expected behaviour: DOR1 advances on each TIM15 update, the DMA refills DHR1 cleanly, the sine waveform appears on PA4. Switching back to TSEL1 = 0001 (TIM1_TRGO) silences the chain again.

Software trigger (TSEL1 = 0000, then pulse DAC1->SWTRIGR = 1) also works: DOR1 follows DHR1 on each pulse. So the DAC's trigger acceptance mechanism is functional — only the specific TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal route is silent.

## Suspected root cause

Either:
- A device-header off-by-one in the DAC_TRIGGER_T1_TRGO macro encoding (analogous to the ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos issue in #69), where the TSEL1 value 0001 actually maps to a different (silent) trigger source on this silicon than the HAL believes.
- Or a silicon-level routing issue between TIM1's TRGO output and the DAC1 trigger input mux, possibly requiring an additional enable bit somewhere outside the DAC's own CR.

I haven't been able to discriminate between these without ST's RTL or trigger-mux documentation. The diagnostic steps above are sufficient to reproduce the silent-trigger symptom; the fix requires ST internal information.

## Workaround

metadata.issue_title: TIM1_TRGO → DAC1 internal trigger route is silent on STM32U5A5JTxQ — DAC sees no triggers despite correct CR config

text: Substitute a different timer's TRGO (e.g. TIM15_TRGO via TSEL1 = 1000). Verified working at 1 kHz with the rest of the chain unchanged.

Title: LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.EXTSEL = 5 correctly set

Body:
# LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.EXTSEL = 5 correctly set

**Related:** depends on the workaround from issue #69 (override CFGR1.EXTSEL in user code) being applied first — without it EXTSEL is 010 (TIM2_TRGO) instead of 101 (LPTIM1_CH1) and this bug is masked by the wrong-trigger symptom.

**Repository:** STM32CubeU5 (HAL or device header — exact root cause not isolated)

**Versions affected:**

- CMSIS device: V1.4.2.0
- HAL: V1.6.x
- Affected chip: STM32U5A5JTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q

## Severity

ADC4 with LPTIM1_CH1 trigger source never starts converting, even though LPTIM1 internally completes compare-match events. The LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 EXT trigger route is silent. Any low-power "sample-then-sleep" pattern that depends on this combination fails to capture data in Stop modes.

## Bench evidence

Project setup:

metadata.issue_title: LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.EXTSEL = 5 correctly set

text:
- ADC4 activated, channel 4 (PC3) enabled.
- hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConv = ADC4_EXTERNALTRIG_LPTIM1_CH1
- hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConvEdge = ADC_EXTERNALTRIGCONVEDGE_RISING
- After HAL_ADC_Init, ADC4->CFGR1 is overridden in user code to write the correct EXTSEL bits at silicon position 5-7 (workaround for the separate ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one filed under issue #N).
- LPTIM1: kernel clock = LSE 32.768 kHz (verified — RCC->BDCR=0x883 with LSEON=1, LSERDY=1; CCIPR3 LPTIM1SEL = 0b11 = LSE), Init.Period = 32767, channel-1 PWM via HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel(.Pulse=32700, .OCPolarity=LPTIM_OCPOLARITY_HIGH) + HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start(&hlptim1, LPTIM_CHANNEL_1).
- LPDMA1 channel 2 allocated for ADC4, circular DMA, 10-sample buffer.

Runtime register dump (CPU active, no Stop entry):

metadata.issue_title: LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.EXTSEL = 5 correctly set

text:
ADC4->CFGR1 = 0x002005a3   (EXTSEL bits 5..7 = 0b101 = 5 = LPTIM1_CH1)
LPTIM1->CR  = 0x1          (ENABLE set, running)
LPTIM1->ARR = 32767        (matches Init.Period)
LPTIM1->CCR1 = 32700       (matches HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel.Pulse)
LPTIM1->CCMR1 = 0x2        (CCE = 1, channel-1 enabled, output-compare mode, polarity active high)
LPTIM1->ISR  = 0x118       (bits 3=CMPM1, 4=ARROK, 8=UE — compare match HAS fired)
                           (bit 0=CMP1OK = 0  ← never sets)
                           (bit 1=ARRM   = 0  ← never sets even after seconds)
RCC->BDCR   = 0x883        (LSEON, LSERDY)
RCC->CCIPR3 = 0x4f83       (LPTIM1SEL bits 10-11 = 0b11 = LSE)

LPTIM1 CNT was confirmed to advance at the LSE rate by polling: 0 → 3284 over 100 ms (expected ~3276 at 32.768 kHz, well within crystal tolerance).

### What's puzzling about the ISR state

metadata.issue_title: LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.EXTSEL = 5 correctly set

text:
- CMPM1 (bit 3 — compare match flag) **does set**, so the comparator is running and matching CCR1.
- CMP1OK (bit 0 — CMP1 register update acknowledged) **never sets**, even after explicitly clearing via ICR and re-writing LPTIM1->CCR1 = 32700 with the timer enabled.
- ARRM (bit 1 — autoreload match) **never sets** even though the period (~32768 LSE ticks ≈ 1 s) elapses many times.

The combination — internal compare matches happen, but the "register update acknowledged" handshake never completes and the autoreload-match flag never latches — suggests the LPTIM-side register-update / event-output path is in some non-standard state.

### What does work

- ADC4 + TIM2_TRGO (the trigger ADC4 *actually* sees when CubeMX/HAL writes the wrong CFGR1 — see the EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one report) does deliver triggers and ADC4 converts.
- LPTIM1 ARRM IRQ wakes the CPU correctly when used the conventional way (HAL_LPTIM_Counter_Start_IT) — independently verified.

So both endpoints work in isolation. Only the chained LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 EXT path fails to deliver.

## What I have not isolated

I haven't been able to pin down whether the bug is:

metadata.issue_title: LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path: ADC4 never converts even with CFGR1.EXTSEL = 5 correctly set

text:
1. A LPTIM HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel / HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start ordering bug that leaves CMP1 in a half-initialized state.
2. An internal silicon route between LPTIM1's compare-match output and the ADC4 trigger input that needs a separate enable bit not exposed via the HAL.
3. A second device-header off-by-one that affects either the LPTIM CCMR1 or the ADC4 trigger-mux register.

The minimal repro outlined above is sufficient to reproduce the symptom; isolating between (1)/(2)/(3) would require either ST's RTL/silicon documentation or scope traces of the LPTIM1_CH1 internal trigger line (not externally observable).

## Workaround currently in use

CPU-mediated 1 Hz sampling: LPTIM1's ARRM IRQ wakes the CPU each second, the CPU triggers a single ADC4 conversion via HAL_ADC_Start(&hadc4), reads the value, stores it, and re-enters Stop 2. Power consumption is slightly higher than a true autonomous chain (CPU briefly active each cycle) but the sample-then-sleep pattern still demonstrates µA-class operation.

Title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

Body:
# stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

**Repository:** STM32CubeU5 (the device header is bundled here; root cause may be in cmsis_device_u5)

**Versions affected:**

- CMSIS device: __STM32U5_CMSIS_VERSION = V1.4.2.0 (per stm32u5xx.h lines 94-101)
- HAL: __STM32U5xx_HAL_VERSION_MAIN = 0x01, _SUB1 = 0x06 → V1.6.x (per stm32u5xx_hal.c lines 57-58)
- Affected chip: STM32U5A5JTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q (stm32u5a5xx.h)

## Severity

**Silent miscompile of every ADC4 trigger-source selection.** The HAL writes the trigger-source bits into the wrong positions of ADC4->CFGR1. Code that asks for ADC4_EXTERNALTRIG_LPTIM1_CH1 ends up with EXTSEL field set to 0b010 = TIM2_TRGO. If TIM2 happens to be active in the project, ADC4 fires on its events at high rate; if not, ADC4 silently sees no triggers. Both failure modes are hard to diagnose because nothing returns HAL_ERROR.

## Root cause — single off-by-one in the device header

metadata.issue_title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

text:
Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32U5xx/Include/stm32u5a5xx.h, lines 3852-3857:

c
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos               (6UL)
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk               (0x7UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)    /*!< 0x000003E0 */
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL                   ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_0                 (0x01UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)   /*!< 0x00000020 */
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_1                 (0x02UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)   /*!< 0x00000040 */
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_2                 (0x04UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)   /*!< 0x00000080 */

The comments next to the constants — 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0x3E0 — are correct values for Pos = 5. The actual preprocessor expansion uses Pos = 6, producing **0x40, 0x80, 0x100** (one bit too far left) and a mask of **0x1C0** (not 0x3E0). The _Msk comment compounds the contradiction by claiming 0x000003E0 while the macro evaluates to 0x000001C0.

For comparison, the equivalent ADC1 group at lines 3793-3800 uses ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos = 5UL and the comments match the macro values:

metadata.issue_title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

text:
c
#define ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos               (5UL)
#define ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk               (0x1FUL << ADC_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)     /*!< 0x000003E0 */
...

ADC1 is correct; ADC4 has the typo.

## What goes wrong downstream

Drivers/STM32U5xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32u5xx_ll_adc.h builds ADC4 trigger-source values from these constants. For example:

c
#define LL_ADC_REG_TRIG_EXT_LPTIM1_CH1_ADC4 \
    (ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_2 | ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_0 | ADC_REG_TRIG_EXT_EDGE_DEFAULT)

- **Comment-implied value** (Pos=5): 0x80 | 0x20 | 0x400 = 0x4A0 → EXTSEL=5 (LPTIM1_CH1) + EXTEN rising
- **Actual macro value** (Pos=6): 0x100 | 0x40 | 0x400 = 0x540 → bit 8 (Reserved) + bit 6 (EXTSEL[1]) + bit 10 (EXTEN rising)

HAL_ADC_Init ORs the (wrong) value into CFGR1 directly. The silicon reads the EXTSEL field from bits 5-7, sees 0b010 = 2, and routes the trigger from TIM2_TRGO instead of LPTIM1_CH1.

Same arithmetic shift applies to every other LL trigger-source macro in the ADC4 group (TIM1_TRGO2, TIM1_CH4, TIM2_TRGO, TIM15_TRGO, TIM6_TRGO, LPTIM1_CH1, LPTIM3_CH2, EXTI_LINE15). Every one of them lands in the wrong CFGR1 bits.

## Bench reproduction

NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q with a project where:

metadata.issue_title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

text:
- ADC4 is activated, channel 4 (PC3) enabled
- hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConv = ADC4_EXTERNALTRIG_LPTIM1_CH1
- hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConvEdge = ADC_EXTERNALTRIGCONVEDGE_RISING
- LPTIM1 configured: kernel clock = LSE 32.768 kHz, ARR = 32767, CCR1 = 32700, channel-1 PWM started via HAL_LPTIM_OC_ConfigChannel + HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start
- LPDMA1 channel allocated for ADC4, circular DMA, S = 10 samples

Read at runtime *after* HAL_ADC_Init:

hadc4.Init.ExternalTrigConv = 0x00000540   ← should be 0x000004A0
ADC4->CFGR1                = 0x00200543    ← EXTSEL bits 5..7 = 0b010 = TIM2_TRGO

If TIM2 is also active in the project (it commonly is — TIM2 is the standard input-capture timer in early labs), the ADC4 chain captures all 10 samples in well under one second instead of the expected ten seconds. Disabling the user-code call to HAL_LPTIM_PWM_Start does **not** stop the conversions — proof that the trigger source is something other than LPTIM1.

Forcing EXTSEL = 5 directly:

c
ADC4->CFGR1 = (ADC4->CFGR1 & ~(0x7UL << 5)) | (0x5UL << 5);

metadata.issue_title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

text:
restores the correct trigger-source field, but no triggers reach ADC4 in this configuration — there is a separate issue with the LPTIM1_CH1 → ADC4 trigger path that this report does not cover (LPTIM1's CMP1OK flag never sets even though CMPM1 does fire internally).

## Suggested fix

diff
-#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos               (6UL)
-#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk               (0x7UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)
+#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos               (5UL)
+#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk               (0x7UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)

After the fix, ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Msk evaluates to 0xE0 (matching the actual silicon field at bits 5-7 — note the existing /*!< 0x000003E0 */ comment overstates the field width and should also be updated to 0x000000E0).

Verified: writing the corrected EXTSEL=5 value (0xA0) into the EXTSEL field of CFGR1 directly is what the LL macros need to produce.

## Workaround for downstream code

Until the header is fixed, projects that select an ADC4 trigger source must override CFGR1.EXTSEL after HAL_ADC_Init:

metadata.issue_title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

text:
c
HAL_ADC_Init(&hadc4);
/* Workaround for ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos off-by-one in stm32u5a5xx.h: write
 * the EXTSEL field at its correct silicon position (bits 5..7).  Replace
 * the literal 0x5 with 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 per the trigger source you want. */
ADC4->CFGR1 = (ADC4->CFGR1 & ~(0x7UL << 5)) | (0x5UL << 5);

metadata.issue_title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

text:
What remains is a smaller documentation inconsistency in the same header section. The inline comments next to the four EXTSEL lines in Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32U5xx/Include/stm32u5a5xx.h show values that correspond to _Pos = 5 (the ADC1-style 5-bit layout), not the actual _Pos = 6 3-bit layout:

c
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos               (6UL)

#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_1                 (0x02UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)   /*!< 0x00000040 */
#define ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_2                 (0x04UL << ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos)   /*!< 0x00000080 */

The actual evaluated values with _Pos = 6 are:

| Line | Comment says | Macro evaluates to |
|---|---|---|
| _Msk     | 0x000003E0 | 0x000001C0 |
| _EXTSEL_0 | 0x00000020 | 0x00000040 |
| _EXTSEL_1 | 0x00000040 | 0x00000080 |
| _EXTSEL_2 | 0x00000080 | 0x00000100 |

metadata.issue_title: stm32u5a5xx.h: ADC4_CFGR1_EXTSEL_Pos is 6, should be 5 — every ADC4 trigger source silently maps to the wrong CFGR1 bits

text:
The macros compile to the right values, so this isn't a functional bug — but the inline comments are a readability trap for anyone reading the header to confirm bit positions against the RM. It looks like the ADC4 block was copy-pasted from the ADC1 EXTSEL group (a few hundred lines earlier in the same file, which uses _Pos = 5 with these exact comment values), and the _Pos was updated to 6 but the comments weren't.

Suggested fix: update the four comments to match the macro values produced by _Pos = 6.

Title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

Body:
# LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

## Summary

When an LPBAM scenario contains an **I2C Master_Transmit node** with the DevAddress field set to a 7-bit slave address (the value the CubeMX scenario designer accepts), the actual address byte transmitted on the I2C bus is **not** the expected value. The I2C peripheral sends an address byte that the slave does not recognise, so the slave does not ACK, no data is exchanged, and the response buffer stays at its uninitialised value forever.

This appears to be an interaction between (a) the CubeMX scenario designer's input validation (which accepts only 7-bit values, max 127) and (b) the LPBAM library's CR2.SADD encoding in STM32CubeU5/Utilities/lpbam/STM32U5/stm32_ll_lpbam.c (which OR's the raw DevAddress value into CR2 without shifting).

## Affected versions

- STM32CubeU5 firmware: as included in STM32CubeMX 6.17 (verified locally May 2026)
- Target: STM32U5A5ZJTxQ on NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q
- TrustZone: disabled (the bug is independent of TZ)

## Reproduction project

metadata.issue_title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

text:
Minimal CubeMX project, ~200 lines of user code, single I2C3 peripheral.

### CubeMX setup

- Board Selector: NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q
- TrustZone: **Disabled**
- HSE: Crystal/Resonator (16 MHz, X3 on-board crystal)
- PLL → SYSCLK 160 MHz, Range 1, EPOD on
- Peripherals enabled:
  - **USART1** (Async, 115200 8N1, PA9/PA10 for VCP)
  - **I2C3** (Standard mode 100 kHz, PC0/PC1, **autonomous mode disabled**)
  - **LPTIM1** (Counter mode, ARR=32767)
  - **LPDMA1** Channel 1
- LPBAM Application "LpbamAp1" with one queue containing 3 nodes:
  1. LPTIM1.Start (continuous mode)
  2. I2C3.MasterTx — 1 byte, **DevAddress = 80 (0x50)**, no LPDMA trigger, AUTOEND, 7-bit
  3. I2C3.MasterRx — 8 bytes, **DevAddress = 80 (0x50)**, LPDMA trigger = LPTIM1 CH1 rising, AUTOEND, 7-bit

### Hardware

- AT24C02 EEPROM (DIP-8) on I2C3:
  - Pin 1-3 (A0/A1/A2): GND → slave address 0x50
  - Pin 4: GND
  - Pin 5 (SDA): PC1 (CN9-9)
  - Pin 6 (SCL): PC0 (CN9-11)
  - Pin 7 (WP): GND
  - Pin 8 (VCC): 3V3

Internal pull-ups enabled in user code on PC0/PC1 (~40 kΩ — adequate for 100 kHz).

### Linker script + manual edits required to make the project build

metadata.issue_title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

text:
CubeMX 6.17 generates an incomplete LPBAM scenario for this configuration:
1. **lpbam_lpbamap1_scenario_config.c is not generated** — the header declares MX_LpbamAp1_Scenario_Init/Link/Start but no implementation exists. We hand-wrote stub implementations.
2. **__attribute__((section(".lpbam_section"))) is not applied** to the LPBAM node descriptors — they land in main SRAM (0x20...) instead of SRAM4 (0x28...). Added manually inside the USER CODE BEGIN Queue*_Desc blocks (regen-survivable).
3. **extern declarations** for the user data buffers (lpbam_cmd, lpbam_resp defined in main.c) had to be added in scenario_build.c USER CODE EV block.
4. **Linker script SRAM4 section** (.lpbam_section (NOLOAD) >SRAM4) added manually.

Each of those four items is arguably a separate CubeMX shortcoming. The bug below is independent of all of them — once the buffers and descriptors are confirmed in SRAM4, the address-encoding bug still occurs.

## Expected vs Actual

### Expected (based on standard CubeMX I2C semantics)

metadata.issue_title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

text:
Setting DevAddress = 80 (= 0x50, the 7-bit AT24C02 address — the value the GUI accepts as a valid 7-bit address) should result in the I2C peripheral transmitting the address byte 0xA0 (= 0x50 << 1 with R/W=0) on the bus. The AT24C02 ACKs, and the chain proceeds.

### Actual

A logic-analyzer capture of the bus shows the address byte decoded as 0x00 (general-call address). The AT24C02 does not ACK its own address (which is 0x50, not 0x00). The data byte the master attempts to send (the EEPROM memory pointer 0x00) is NACK'd along with the address. The response buffer lpbam_resp is never updated.

### VCP output (after power-cycle to clear SRAM)

=== LPBAM single-byte MasterTx repro ===
I2C3 scan: 0x50
EEPROM page-write [C0..C7] @ 0x00: HAL=0
EEPROM verify-read: HAL=0, bytes = C0 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7
LPBAM scenario built: 15 nodes starting at 0x2800000C
Buffer addrs: lpbam_cmd=0x28000000  lpbam_resp=0x28000004  (SRAM4 = 0x28xxxxxx)
LPBAM started — observing chain output:
cycle 1: B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F
cycle 2: B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F
cycle 3: B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F

metadata.issue_title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

text:
The B0 B2 E0 1F 31 D3 CD 2F is uninitialised SRAM4 garbage that never gets overwritten by the LPBAM chain. The pre-pop verify confirms the EEPROM is wired correctly and contains C0..C7 at addresses 0..7 — the LPBAM read just isn't reaching it.

### Bus decode

write to 0x00 ack data: 0x00

Each LPTIM1 cycle the bus shows two transactions: a 2-byte write to address 0x00 followed by an 8-byte read attempt that returns no ACKs.

## Root-cause analysis (preliminary)

Looking at Utilities/lpbam/STM32U5/stm32_ll_lpbam.c line 1131:

c
case LPBAM_I2C_CONFIG_TRANSACTION_ID:
{
  ...
  dummy = pConfNode->pInstance->CR2;                       // line 1122
  *pConfNode->NodeDesc.pSrcVarReg = dummy | I2C_CR2_STOP;  // line 1125
  if ((mode is master)) {
    dummy |= I2C_CR2_START | I2C_CR2_RELOAD | I2C_CR2_AUTOEND
           | I2C_CR2_RD_WRN | pConfNode->Config.DevAddress  // line 1131
           | ((uint32_t)pConfNode->Config.Size << I2C_CR2_NBYTES_Pos);
    ...
    if (master TX) dummy &= ~I2C_CR2_RD_WRN;               // line 1265
    dummy |= AddressingMode << I2C_CR2_ADD10_Pos;          // line 1269
    *pConfNode->NodeDesc.pSrcVarReg = dummy | DevAddress;  // line 1272
  }
}

metadata.issue_title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

text:
The library OR's DevAddress directly into CR2's lower bits (SADD[9:0]). For 7-bit addressing, the I2C peripheral expects the actual 7-bit address in SADD[7:1] (i.e. shifted left by 1). With DevAddress=80 the SADD field ends up = 0x50, which the peripheral interprets as SADD[7:1] = 0x28 → bus byte = 0x50/0x51 → an analyzer would decode this as 7-bit address 0x28, not the intended 0x50.

But the bus trace decodes as 0x00, not 0x28 — so there is *additional* corruption beyond just the missing left-shift. Possibilities: the write at line 1125 (dummy | I2C_CR2_STOP, which has SADD bits zero) is going to the same descriptor and clobbering the SADD bits set at line 1272; or a separate later descriptor re-writes CR2 with stale STOP bits; or the I2C peripheral responds to the multi-step LPDMA write sequence in a way that ends with SADD cleared.

metadata.issue_title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

text:
We did **not** fully isolate which of these is at fault. Manually patching DevAddress to a pre-shifted value (e.g. 0xA0 for slave 0x50) bakes the descriptor's CR2 source value correctly in SRAM (verified by reading the LPBAM source words after MX_*_Scenario_Build) — yet the bus still shows an incorrect address. Something at runtime, after LPDMA writes the descriptor's source value to CR2, is corrupting the SADD field.

## Workaround

Restrict LPBAM I2C scenarios to **MasterRx-only** chains (single-node, hardware-triggered). Reading from a peripheral that doesn't require an address-pointer write avoids the MasterTx node entirely. The bug above prevents any single-byte MasterTx from completing successfully on the bus.

## Asks of ST

metadata.issue_title: LPBAM I2C MasterTx silently writes wrong SADD on bus (STM32CubeU5)

text:
1. Document the DevAddress encoding convention expected by the LPBAM I2C node — is it raw (already shifted) or 7-bit (lib should shift)?
2. Fix the CubeMX scenario designer to (a) accept the matching encoding and (b) reject invalid values upfront.
3. Fix the runtime address corruption that causes bus to show 0x00 even when the descriptor's SADD bits are correct in SRAM.
4. Make the manual fixes listed above (scenario_config.c generation, NODE_SECTION attribute, extern decls, linker section) part of CubeMX's standard LPBAM output.

> 0: LPTIM is disabled. Writing '0' to the ENABLE bit **resets all the DMA request signals (input capture

https://github.com/stm32duino/STM32LowPower/commit/d2303da65831f1c4aeaafe7bc89833406a106ef8

Perhaps creating an alias in stm32u5xx_ll_pwr.h would preserve backward compatibility while bringing alignment on LL_PWR_MODE_STOP2 across all HALs.

Title: The LPBAM scenario fails to be created after the HAL update.

Body:
**Setup Description**:
We used a circular LPBAM setup involving 
LPDMA, LPADC, LPTIM, and LPGPIO peripherals.

**Bug Description**:
As stated in the title, the LPBAM application 
scenario fails to be successfully created after 
updating the STM32U5 HAL from v1.5.0 to v1.7.0 (STM32CubeU5).

**Steps to Reproduce**:
Initializing the LPBAM circular application.

**Expected Behavior**:
The LPBAM circular application should be successfully created.

**Observed Behavior**:
The LPBAM application fails to be created successfully, showing an error 
indicating that the node cannot be found when setting LPBAM circular mode 
to a linked-list queue based on the selected descriptor and node level.

metadata.issue_title: The LPBAM scenario fails to be created after the HAL update.

text:
Call hierarchy to error:
 - LPBAM_Status_t ADV_LPBAM_Q_SetCircularMode(...)
 - HAL_DMAEx_List_SetCircularModeConfig(...)
 - DMA_List_FindNode(...)
 - if (currentnode_address != ((uint32_t)pNode & DMA_CLLR_LA))
 
Additionally, an interesting observation is that when compiler 
optimizations are enabled (tested with size optimization and debug optimization), 
the function ADV_LPBAM_Q_SetCircularMode(...) returns an error. 
However, when optimizations are disabled, the function does not return 
an error, but the result remains the same—the LPBAM peripherals mentioned 
above do not function as expected.

**Additional Explanation**:
If we move ADV_LPBAM_Q_SetCircularMode immediately after setting 
the node as the start of the circular linked list, the function 
successfully finds the node and sets it as the start of the list. 
However, we still encounter issues with other LPBAM peripherals 
used in this application.

During debugging, we identified a few lines of code that were 
modified between HAL versions and appear to introduce this issue. 
When these lines are commented out, everything functions as expected. 
We would like to clarify their exact purpose.

text:

- File: stm32u5xx_hal_dma_ex.c  
- Function: DMA_List_BuildNode(...)

While it's clear that these lines were added to reset the node during 
initialization, could it be possible that the previous node in the 
linked list is being overwritten during the creation of the circular

 * Project created using STM32CubeMX 6.11.0, using STM32CubeU5 v1.15.0

**Describe the bug (skip if none)**

When setting up USBX in STM32CubeMX with STM32CubeU5 in MSC mode, if I set UX_SLAVE_REQUEST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH to any value other than 4096, then there is a #define directive in USBX/App/ux_user.h, however if I set it to exactly 4096, that line is commented out.

The problem is that [Middlewares/ST/usbx/ports/generic/inc/ux_port.h](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Middlewares/ST/usbx/ports/generic/inc/ux_port.h#L200) has code that defaults UX_SLAVE_REQUEST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH to 2048 if it isn't set.

text:
Putting those two things together means that if I set UX_SLAVE_REQUEST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH to 4096 in STM32CubeMX, the actual value in my code will be 2048.

**How to reproduce the bug (skip if none)**

1. Create a project in STM32CubeMX using STM32CubeU5
2. Enable USBX for the project in slave MSC mode
3. Set UX_SLAVE_REQUEST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH to 4096 in STM32CubeMX
4. Generate sources
5. Run the project
6. Notice that the actual value of UX_SLAVE_REQUEST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH is 2048 despite what was set in STM32CubeMX

**Additional context**

I was able to find a workaround by defining a custom constant UX_SLAVE_REQUEST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH for USBX (which creates the constant in main.h), then update USBX/App/ux_user.h to add #include "main.h" in the USER CODE BEGIN 1 part.

Body:
stm32u5xx_hal_cryp

We use AES in byte mode (CRYP_DATATYPE_8B).

CRYP_ConfigTypeDef provides the option to set the DataType. This works fine for the data fed into AES but KEY & IV are passed in in mode CRYP_DATATYPE_32B regardless of the setup of DataType.

see static void CRYP_SetIV(CRYP_HandleTypeDef *hcryp) & static void CRYP_SetKey(CRYP_HandleTypeDef *hcryp, uint32_t KeySize).

This is especially problematic since key & iv are not passed to the hardware registers during HAL_CRYP_Init or HAL_CRYP_SetConfig but when calling HAL_CRYP_Encrypt which means we can't use local (stack) variables to correct the data alignment ourselves.

Please update CRYP_SetIV & CRYP_SetKey so they can deal with all modes of DataType.

Thanks,
Manuel

Title: Polling USB interrupt endpoints at 1 ms intervals doesn't work

Body:
**Describe the set-up**

- STM32U575I-EV evaluation board
- STM32CubeU5 1.4.0
- STM32CubeIDE 1.14.1

**Describe the bug (skip if none)**

USB endpoints that declare a 1 ms polling interval are not correctly handled by the USBX STM32 host controller driver.

**How to reproduce the bug (skip if none)**

1. Program the Ux_Host_HID example to the board and configure the board jumpers.
2. Attach a Low Speed mouse to the host port and observe expected behaviour - interrupt endpoint is polled every 8 ms with data being returned when available.
3. Attach a Full Speed mouse with an endpoint that has a 1 ms pollinig interval to the host port.  The interrupt endpoint stops being polled after the first NAK.

Note that this is not limited to Ux_Host_HID or HID devices.  It affects any USB endpoint that sets a 1 ms periodic interval.

**Additional context**

Investigation shows that when the endpoint is created the interval mask is set as 0 as expected to force the scheduler to queue the host channel every frame.  In _ux_hcd_stm32_perioidic_schedule() the scheduler mode is set:

metadata.issue_title: Polling USB interrupt endpoints at 1 ms intervals doesn't work

text:
c
/* If it's scheduled each SOF/uSOF, the request should be submitted
* immediately after packet is done. This is performed in callback.  */
if (ed -> ux_stm32_ed_interval_mask == 0)
  ed -> ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode = 0;

However, HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback() does not appear to handle the case where urb_state == URB_NOTREADY and ed -> ux_stm32_ed_type == EP_TYPE_INTR (and possibly EP_TYPE_ISOC) so the transmit request is never resubmitted.

Comments:
[ALABSTM - 2024-02-06T12:49:25Z]
Hi @wooyay,

The HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback() is supposed to be **customized by users** depending on the needs of their applications.
In your case, are you referring to the __weak callback at the [driver level](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/f1946d68701260860cdb5eae9f7bc5c3ff7f1cd1/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_hcd.c#L733-L743) or to a redefined one in one of the of the [USBx applications](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/tree/main/Projects/STM32U575I-EV/Applications/USBX) provided within this firmware?

Regarding the handling of the case urb_state == URB_NOTREADY, it seems handled at the middleware library level, as shown below:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/c8fcb26ff629cf7c2a3b2c60e6121625eaa5ca2d/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_callback.c#L421-L435

Regarding endpoint types EP_TYPE_INTR and EP_TYPE_ISOC handling in case urb_state == URB_NOTREADY, they are handled at driver level in function HAL_HCD_HC_SubmitRequest() as you can see from [this](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/f1946d68701260860cdb5eae9f7bc5c3ff7f1cd1/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_hcd.c#L474-L504) code snippet.

Hi @ALABSTM,

metadata.issue_title: Polling USB interrupt endpoints at 1 ms intervals doesn't work

text: I realise HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback() is a function to be implemented, but in the case of the USBx applications this has already been done by the [USBx STM32 host controller driver](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_callback.c#L207).  As previously said, if you run the [Ux_Host_HID](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/tree/main/Projects/STM32U575I-EV/Applications/USBX/Ux_Host_HID) example with no modifications and attach a mouse device with a 1 ms polling interval you will see the host poll the endpoint until the first NAK is returned from the device and then no further attempts to poll.  This does not affect slower devices with polling intervals of 2 ms or more.

metadata.issue_title: Polling USB interrupt endpoints at 1 ms intervals doesn't work

text:
When interrupt [endpoints are created](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_endpoint_create.c#L79) the polling interval mask is calculated based on the interval given in the endpoint descriptor:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/c8fcb26ff629cf7c2a3b2c60e6121625eaa5ca2d/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_endpoint_create.c#L199-L202
In the case of a typical Low Speed mouse with a endpoint polling interval of 10 ms ux_stm32_ed_interval_mask is calculated as 7, so the endpoint is polled every 8 frames.  A Full Speed mouse with a endpoint polling interval of 1 ms sets ux_stm32_ed_interval_mask to 0 so it must be polled every frame.

metadata.issue_title: Polling USB interrupt endpoints at 1 ms intervals doesn't work

text:
Interrupt endpoints are typically submitted by the [periodic scheduler](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_periodic_schedule.c#L78) which is triggered by the SOF interrupt.  The periodic scheduler compares the current frame number against the interrupt mask to decide whether HAL_HCD_HC_SubmitRequest() should be called but only if ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode != 0.  If the interval mask is 0, as set for 1 ms endpoints, ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode is never set:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/c8fcb26ff629cf7c2a3b2c60e6121625eaa5ca2d/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_periodic_schedule.c#L201-L208
**1 ms endpoints must be scheduled by the callback as stated in the comment.**

metadata.issue_title: Polling USB interrupt endpoints at 1 ms intervals doesn't work

text:
If the transfer completes with a NAK, the [callback function](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/main/Middlewares/ST/usbx/common/usbx_stm32_host_controllers/ux_hcd_stm32_callback.c#L207) is called with urb_state == URB_NOTREADY.  For all interrupt endpoints the callback **does not** reschedule the transfer by calling HAL_HCD_HC_SubmitRequest().  This is expected for endpoints with a polling interval of more than 1 ms as ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode == 1 and so the periodic scheduler will handle this on a later SOF interrupt.  For 1 ms endpoints they are never handled as HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback() doesn't call HAL_HCD_HC_SubmitRequest()and the periodic scheduler will ignore them because ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode == 0.

In the code from the callback handling urb_state == URB_NOTREADY another case needs to be added to handle EP_TYPE_INTR where ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode == 0 to resubmit the transfer either by calling HAL_HCD_HC_SubmitRequest() again to by forcing the periodic scheduler to submit the transfer by setting ux_stm32_ed_sch_mode = 1.

From what I see from your last test, although your USB OTG HS clock is fed by the HSE clock, your PLL1P is still fed by the MSIS. Hence, the same issue and the timeout.

According to our development teams, the recommendation is to use the HSE clock for the USB OTG HS. An alternative is the HSE clock bypass mode using an external clock source. This would allow you to use only the OSC_IN pin and spare the OSC_OUT. You can refer to the reference manual for more details.

I am not sure whether the HSI clock would be any of a solution. However, our development teams strongly discourage such option. I hope this helps.

With regards,

We are still investigating to find the root cause. We will provide a fix in a future release.

In the meantime, I suggest to use a Data Memory Barrier (DMB) as a workaround. 
By inserting it between the access to ADC_CR_CALINDEX and ADC_CALFACT2 and again before the access to ADC_CALFACT.

MODIFY_REG(hadc->Instance->CR, ADC_CR_CALINDEX, 0x9UL << ADC_CR_CALINDEX_Pos);
__DMB();
MODIFY_REG(hadc->Instance->CALFACT2, 0x00FF0000UL, 0x00020000UL);
__DMB();
SET_BIT(hadc->Instance->CALFACT, ADC_CALFACT_LATCH_COEF);

Title: DMA_SetConfig() function call not backward compatible with STM32L4 HAL

Body:
This isn't a bug as such, but it is a trap for anyone porting from STM32L4 (and maybe other older STM32s) to the U5 HAL.

The parameter SrcDataSize in the function DMA_SetConfig() has a different meaning from STM32L4 - this is due to the difference between the U5 GPDMA GPDMA_CxBR1 register BNDT field - which is the number of _bytes_ to transfer (RM0456 17.8.12) and the L4 DMA DMA_CNDTRx register NDT field which is the number of _DMA transfers_ (RM0432, 11.6.4).

If the source and destination datawidths are both bytes then DMA_SetConfig() functions identically on the U5 and L4, but if the datawidth is half-word or word then on the U5 the DMA transfer ends after either 1/2 or 1/4 of the DMA is complete since each transfer counts for 2 or 4 bytes,

static void DMA_SetConfig(DMA_HandleTypeDef const *const hdma,
                          uint32_t SrcAddress,
                          uint32_t DstAddress,
                          uint32_t SrcDataSize)   <<< this parameter is a byte count on the U5 and a transfer count on L4

metadata.issue_title: DMA_SetConfig() function call not backward compatible with STM32L4 HAL

text:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/2e2b3e4733ddcde7af1e91f1c27ef7bea84389ce/Drivers/STM32U5xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_dma.c#L1588

This difference in functionality affects any callers of either HAL_DMA_Start() or HAL_DMA_Start_IT().
It's possible to fix this with conditional compilation in the application code, but it's not ideal to have a near identical HAL API with different functionality.  In theory DMA_SetConfig() could read the burst length configured in the hdma struct and multiply the SrcDataSize accordingly and I think that this would lead to a consistent API behavior on the U5 to the L4 - but perhaps it's too late to make this change since it would likely break existing applications.  Perhaps a comment above the function prototypes to draw attention to the difference ?

Title: DAC related HAL functions stalling when timebase interrupts are disabled

Body:
**Describe the set-up**

* This behavior is platform independent
 * Arm GNU Toolchain 12.2.MPACBTI-Bet1

**Describe the bug**

Additional delays are inserted in some of the DAC HAL functions, which make use of HAL_Delay timebase function, whose purpose is supposedly avoiding fast switching of the DAC peripheral state, thus enforcing a minimum delay between various operations.
Not only can this become cumbersome by itself, as the delay (**1ms**) can be considered quite large in some applications, but the biggest issue at hand is that, should the HAL timebase be temporarily suspended, i.e. because the corresponding timer is paused or the ticker ISR is not called, these functions will completely block the processor in an infinite loop.

Affected functions are:

HAL_DAC_Start()
HAL_DAC_Start_DMA()
HAL_DAC_Stop()
HAL_DAC_Stop_DMA()
HAL_DAC_ConfigChannel()

**How to reproduce the bug (skip if none)**

metadata.issue_title: DAC related HAL functions stalling when timebase interrupts are disabled

text:
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project
    - It is sufficient to have an application making use of the DAC HAL .
2. List the modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Drivers, BSP, MW...)
    -  DAC HAL 
3. Describe the use case that generates the problem
    - Calling one of the aforementioned functions in a context where the HAL timebase counter variable, i.e. **uwTick** doesn't get incremented during the function operation
4. How we can reproduce the problem
    - Recreate context: 
        - Stop the Systick timer, or any timer used for generating the timebase (and thus calling HAL_IncTick on a periodic fashion), or
        - Enter an ISR with an higher priority than the timebase interrupt, or
        - Temporarily disable interrupts
    - Then call one of the aforementioned functions

**Additional context**

It would be sufficient to remove these HAL_Delay functions inside the DAC HAL. This would also remove the cumbersome 1ms delay which is in most cases unneeded. 
It should also be noted that this driver is one of the very few introducing these delays, the other being the USB driver and the OPAMP driver.

ADC oversampling macros incompatible with STM32U575 ADC1  (they are compatible with ADC4)

text:
The STM32L4 ADC oversampling ratio can only be set as a power of 2 (which corresponds  to LL_ADC_OVS_RATIO_X).  From RM0432 section 21.6.5 ADC configuration register 2 (ADC_CFGR2):

Bits 4:2 OVSR[2:0]: Oversampling ratio
This bitfield is set and cleared by software to define the oversampling ratio.
000: 2x
001: 4x
010: 8x
011: 16x
100: 32x
101: 64x
110: 128x
111: 256x

The STM32U5 oversampling ratio is set to any number between 1 and 1024.  From RM0456 section 29.6.5 ADC configuration register 2 (ADC_CFGR2):

Bits 25:16 OSR[9:0]: Oversampling ratio
This bitfield is set and cleared by software to define the oversampling ratio.
0: 1x (no oversampling)
1: 2x
2: 3x
...
1023: 1024x

Therefore the macros ADC_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_X defined in stm32u5xx_hal_adc.h and LL_ADC_OVS_RATIO_X defined in stm32u5xx_ll_adc.h are not compatible with the STM32U575 ADC1 ADC_CRGR2 register - which can cause confusion when porting a project from an older STM32.

metadata.issue_title: ADC oversampling macros incompatible with STM32U575 ADC1  (they are compatible with ADC4)

text:
Note that these macros do appear to be compatible with ADC4 on the STM32U575 - (according to RM0456 30.7.5 ADC configuration register 2 (ADC_CFGR2)) - so perhaps simply renaming the macros in stm32u5xx_hal_adc.h to ADC4_OVERSAMPLING_RATIO_X  would make this clearer.

Title: IOT_HTTP_WebServer application does not send HTTP headers as intended

Body:
**Describe the set-up**

* B-U585I-IOT02A board
 * STM32CubeIDE Version: 1.9.0

**Describe the bug**

The IOT_HTTP_WebServer application does not send HTTP headers as intended.

**How to reproduce the bug**

1. Run the IOT_HTTP_WebServer application on the B-U585I-IOT02A board.
2. Open the "STM32U5 Webserver Demo" website in Chrome.
3. Open the Chrome developer tools and examine the HTTP headers, for example for "chunk.css". 
4. There is no "Response Headers" section present while according to the source code "text/css" should be present as "Content-Type" header, and there should be additional HTTP headers:

![request-chunk css](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98944/163448835-35b12c14-daae-4d72-b9fb-5164a1fcdbe9.png)

Compare that to the response for "chunk.js" which has "Response Headers" including "Content-Type: text/javascript":

![request-chunk js](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98944/163449346-4604982e-2252-4cdf-ab86-8a84cd31b0da.png)

That "chunk.js" has the HTTP headers is purely by coincidence as explained below.

**Additional context**

metadata.issue_title: IOT_HTTP_WebServer application does not send HTTP headers as intended

text:
The problem is caused by the fact that two parameters are passed in the wrong order whenhttp_send_response() calls http_send_headers_response():

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeU5/blob/133d940e5bd3a38955b9ba0cdf316f9681d0af2d/Projects/B-U585I-IOT02A/Demonstrations/IOT_HTTP_WebServer/WebServer/App/http/webserver_http_response.c#L243-L276

Note the call http_send_headers_response(headers_id, socket, headers_buff, data_size), while the signature of http_send_headers_response is http_send_headers_response(uint32_t socket, uint32_t headers_id, ...). The parameters headers_id and socket are passed in the wrong order.

This also explains why the headers for the JavaScript file is sent. It works by accident because the socket id is 1 and because HTTP_HEADER_JS_ID is defined as 1.

The following patch fixes the problem:

metadata.issue_title: IOT_HTTP_WebServer application does not send HTTP headers as intended

text:
diff --git a/Projects/B-U585I-IOT02A/Demonstrations/IOT_HTTP_WebServer/WebServer/App/http/webserver_http_response.c b/Projects/B-U585I-IOT02A/Demonstrations/IOT_HTTP_WebServer/WebServer/App/http/webserver_http_response.c
index dcaf97fd..d04f6251 100644
--- a/Projects/B-U585I-IOT02A/Demonstrations/IOT_HTTP_WebServer/WebServer/App/http/webserver_http_response.c
+++ b/Projects/B-U585I-IOT02A/Demonstrations/IOT_HTTP_WebServer/WebServer/App/http/webserver_http_response.c
@@ -247,7 +247,7 @@ static WebServer_StatusTypeDef http_send_response(uint32_t headers_id,
                                                   uint32_t data_size)
 {
   /* Send HTTP header response */
-  if (http_send_headers_response(headers_id, socket, headers_buff, data_size) != WEBSERVER_OK)
+  if (http_send_headers_response(socket, headers_id, headers_buff, data_size) != WEBSERVER_OK)
   {
     return HTTP_ERROR;
   }

With that patch applied the HTTP headers are sent as expected for all elements.
